clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes an honorary award for distinguished service by civilian officers and employees of the Federal Government, known as the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service, consisting of a gold medal, ribbon and appurtenances, with a suitable inscription and citation on each. The text has no end date. Executive Order 11085 section 2(a) states that other sections of the order are amended conformably to that order, without naming this section; Executive Order 12107 section 2-101 substitutes agency names in the order as amended and this section names no agency; neither changes the words of section 1, which the U.S. Code note prints in its original wording. Operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.reason: Section 2 as originally written has the President present the award to civilian officers or employees for exceptionally meritorious or outstanding civilian service in connection with their official employment, at times the President determines, with not more than five awards in any one year and a group achievement counted as one award. Executive Order 10979 (December 12, 1961) restated section 2 (before: exceptionally meritorious or outstanding service, not more than five awards in any one year; after: the best achievements having current impact in improving Government operations or serving the public interest, exemplifying imagination, courage, high ability or long and distinguished career service, and generally not more than five awards in any one year); this is a rewrite of a whole section that changed the substance, and the clause continues in the restated form. Executive Order 11085 section 2(a) amends other sections conformably without naming this section, and Executive Order 12107 changes no wording of this section. The restated section 2 is printed in the current U.S. Code note. Operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.mechanism: express deletion of the section by amendment (Executive Order 12014)
clauses.reason: Section 3 of the original text was deleted by Executive Order 12014 (42 FR 56105, October 19, 1977), which abolished the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and amended Executive Order 10717 by deleting sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and adding new sections 3 and 4 that assign the advising function to the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission. The executive order has no separate effective-date provision, so the date of signing, October 19, 1977, is used. Before: a Board of five members appointed by the President from the Federal civilian service, with a Chairman designated by the President; Executive Order 11085 section 3 (February 22, 1963) enlarged the Board by five members from outside the Executive Branch for Medal of Freedom purposes, which is an amendment and not an end.

clauses.mechanism: express deletion of the section by amendment (Executive Order 12014)
clauses.reason: Section 8(a) of the original text was deleted by Executive Order 12014 (42 FR 56105, October 19, 1977), which abolished the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and amended Executive Order 10717 by deleting sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and adding new sections 3 and 4 that assign the advising function to the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission. The executive order has no separate effective-date provision, so the date of signing, October 19, 1977, is used. This paragraph (the significance of the contribution must be so outstanding that greater commendation than the head of the employing agency can give is deserved) was listed in section 8 as originally written. Executive Order 10979 (December 12, 1961) restated section 8 without the enumerated criteria and restated section 2 to include a similar standard; the held order does not say that it ended this paragraph, so the first dated end shown by the held text is the deletion of section 8 by Executive Order 12014.

clauses.mechanism: effective-date clause used up when the order took effect on July 1, 1957 (own terms)
clauses.reason: Section 9 states that the order becomes effective on July 1, 1957. It is a one-time effective-date provision that had nothing further to operate once July 1, 1957 arrived, so its own terms end it on that date (the end is recorded on the stated effective day, July 1, 1957). Executive Order 12014 later deleted section 9 along with sections 3 to 8 (October 19, 1977), which confirms the section was no longer part of the order but is not the first end.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10717 of June 27, 1957 (22 FR 4632; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10717.txt, read in full) establishes the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service (sections 1 and 2), the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and its terms, staff, functions, nominations and criteria (sections 3 to 8, with criteria (a) and (b) under section 8), and an effective date of July 1, 1957 (section 9). Later instruments, each read in its held official text: Executive Order 10979 (26 FR 11937, December 12, 1961) restated sections 2, 7 and 8 (substance changed; recorded before and after in the clause reasons); Executive Order 11085 (28 FR 1759, February 22, 1963) enlarged the Board for Medal of Freedom purposes in its section 3, restricted who sits when recommending recipients of this award, and in its section 2(a) restated section 4 on terms of service; Executive Order 12014 (42 FR 56105, October 19, 1977) abolished the Board, deleted sections 3 to 9 and added new sections 3 and 4 vesting the advising function in the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission; Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, December 28, 1978; effective January 1, 1979 under its section 2-404) in section 2-101 substituted the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission and the Director for the Chairman in this order as amended, which changes only the sections added by Executive Order 12014 and no original clause. The Office of the Federal Register disposition note lists these four amendments and no revocation. Sections 1 and 2 remain operative on 2026-10-14: the U.S. Code prints the order as amended (5 U.S.C. 4504 note) and 5 CFR 451.203 implements it. Sections 3 to 9 of the original text ended on October 19, 1977 (section 9, the effective-date clause, was used up when the order took effect on July 1, 1957). Because later amendments restate whole sections, a reviewer should note that section 2 as now in force differs in substance from its 1957 wording. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.

savings.reason: Section 4 of Executive Order 12014 and the surviving sections of Executive Order 10717 now work through the Office of Personnel Management; the awards already made under the original sections and the Board's past recommendations have no continuing legal command and nothing was transferred or accrued that the claim relies on. The deleted Board provisions leave no residual effect: the abolition of the Board in Executive Order 12014 and the substitution of the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission (now the Director of the Office of Personnel Management) show the function moved rather than lapsed.
